questions.text: The chemical symbol of sodium is
questions.explanation: Sodium takes its symbol Na from its Latin name natrium; Ni is the symbol for nickel.

questions.text: The chemical symbol of potassium is
questions.explanation: Potassium is denoted K after its Latin name kalium; P stands for phosphorus and Pt for platinum.

questions.text: The chemical symbol Fe stands for
questions.explanation: Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin name of iron; fluorine is F and francium is Fr.

questions.text: The chemical symbol of gold is
questions.explanation: Gold is written Au from the Latin aurum; Ag is silver and Gd is gadolinium.

questions.text: The chemical symbol Pb belongs to
questions.explanation: Pb is taken from plumbum, the Latin name of lead, which also gives us the word plumbing.

questions.text: The chemical symbol of tin is
questions.explanation: Tin is Sn from the Latin stannum; Ti is titanium and Te is tellurium.

questions.text: The chemical symbol Hg is used for
questions.explanation: Mercury is Hg from hydrargyrum, meaning liquid silver.

questions.text: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust is
questions.explanation: Oxygen makes up roughly 46 per cent of the crust by mass, mainly locked up in silicate and oxide minerals.

questions.text: The most abundant element in the universe is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen accounts for about three quarters of the ordinary matter of the universe by mass.

questions.text: The most abundant metal in the Earth's crust is
questions.explanation: Aluminium is the commonest metal of the crust at about 8 per cent by mass, ahead of iron.

questions.text: The modern periodic law arranges elements in order of increasing
questions.explanation: Properties of elements are periodic functions of atomic number, which resolved the anomalies of the mass-based table.

questions.text: The scientist who established that the properties of elements depend on atomic number was
questions.explanation: Henry Moseley's X-ray studies showed atomic number, not atomic mass, is the fundamental ordering property.

questions.text: Elements of Group 1 of the periodic table are known as
questions.explanation: Lithium, sodium, potassium and their congeners form strongly alkaline hydroxides and are called alkali metals.

questions.text: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine together form the group called
questions.explanation: Group 17 elements are the halogens, a name meaning salt-formers.

questions.text: Helium, neon, argon and krypton belong to the group called
questions.explanation: These Group 18 elements have complete outer electron shells and are chemically very unreactive.

questions.text: The number of periods in the modern periodic table is
questions.explanation: The table has seven horizontal rows, each period corresponding to the filling of a principal energy level.

questions.text: The number of groups in the long form of the periodic table is
questions.explanation: The long form has eighteen vertical columns numbered 1 to 18.

questions.text: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
questions.explanation: Atomic number is defined as the count of protons; the sum of protons and neutrons is the mass number.

questions.text: Isotopes of the same element differ from one another in the number of
questions.explanation: Isotopes share the same proton number but carry different numbers of neutrons, so their mass numbers differ.

questions.text: The most electronegative element is
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of all elements, about 4.0 on the Pauling scale.

questions.text: The lanthanide and actinide series of elements belong to the
questions.explanation: In these two inner transition series the differentiating electron enters an f orbital, so they form the f-block.

questions.text: The only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature is
questions.explanation: Mercury melts at about minus 39 degrees Celsius and so is liquid at room temperature; bromine is a non-metal.

questions.text: The only non-metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature is
questions.explanation: Bromine is a dense reddish-brown liquid; iodine is solid and chlorine is a gas at room temperature.

questions.text: The gas used to fill airships and weather balloons because it is light and non-inflammable is
questions.explanation: Helium has very low density but, unlike hydrogen, does not burn, so it is preferred for lifting balloons.

questions.text: Ordinary incandescent electric bulbs are usually filled with
questions.explanation: Argon is inert and cheap, so it protects the hot tungsten filament from burning away.

questions.text: The gas that gives a bright red-orange glow in advertisement discharge tubes is
questions.explanation: Neon emits the familiar red-orange light in discharge tubes, which is why such signs are called neon signs.

questions.text: The approximate percentage of nitrogen in dry air by volume is
questions.explanation: Dry air is about 78 per cent nitrogen and 21 per cent oxygen by volume.

questions.text: The pH of pure water at 25 degrees Celsius is
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral because the concentrations of hydrogen and hydroxide ions are equal, giving pH 7.

questions.text: Blue litmus paper dipped in an acidic solution turns
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red, while bases turn red litmus blue.

questions.text: The acid present in human gastric juice is
questions.explanation: Parietal cells of the stomach secrete hydrochloric acid, which activates pepsin and kills swallowed microbes.

questions.text: The acid that gives vinegar its sour taste is
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute aqueous solution of acetic acid, usually about 5 to 8 per cent.

questions.text: The acid found in lemons and other citrus fruits is
questions.explanation: Citric acid is the dominant organic acid of citrus fruits and gives them their sharp taste.

questions.text: Souring of milk into curd is caused by the formation of
questions.explanation: Bacteria ferment lactose into lactic acid, which lowers the pH and curdles the milk protein.

questions.text: The irritation caused by an ant sting is due to
questions.explanation: Ants inject formic acid, which takes its name from formica, the Latin word for ant.

questions.text: The acid used as electrolyte in a lead storage battery is
questions.explanation: A lead-acid accumulator uses dilute sulphuric acid between lead and lead dioxide plates.

questions.text: Aqua regia, which dissolves gold, is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in the ratio
questions.explanation: Aqua regia is three parts concentrated hydrochloric acid to one part concentrated nitric acid by volume.

questions.text: Caustic soda is the common name of
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide is called caustic soda because it corrodes skin and other organic matter.

questions.text: Milk of magnesia, taken as an antacid, is a suspension of
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a mild base that neutralises excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

questions.text: The chemical formula of common table salt is
questions.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride, an ionic compound of sodium and chlorine.

questions.text: Baking soda is chemically known as
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3, which releases carbon dioxide on heating and makes dough rise.

questions.text: Washing soda is chemically
questions.explanation: Washing soda is Na2CO3.10H2O, the hydrated form of sodium carbonate used to soften water for laundry.

questions.text: The acid used for etching designs on glass is
questions.explanation: Hydrofluoric acid attacks silica in glass, forming silicon tetrafluoride, so it is used for etching.

questions.text: The chemical formula of limestone is
questions.explanation: Limestone, marble and chalk are all forms of calcium carbonate, CaCO3.

questions.text: Quicklime, obtained by strongly heating limestone, is
questions.explanation: Heating calcium carbonate drives off carbon dioxide and leaves calcium oxide, CaO, called quicklime.

questions.text: Slaked lime has the formula
questions.explanation: Adding water to quicklime gives calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, known as slaked lime.

questions.text: Plaster of Paris is obtained by the controlled heating of
questions.explanation: Gypsum, calcium sulphate dihydrate, loses most of its water at about 120 degrees Celsius to give plaster of Paris.

questions.text: Blue vitriol is the common name of
questions.explanation: Hydrated copper sulphate, CuSO4.5H2O, forms blue crystals and is called blue vitriol.

questions.text: Laughing gas, used as a mild anaesthetic, is
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide, N2O, produces a euphoric effect on inhalation, hence the name laughing gas.

questions.text: Dry ice is the solid form of
questions.explanation: Solid carbon dioxide sublimes directly to gas without wetting anything, so it is called dry ice.

questions.text: The chemical formula of ammonia is
questions.explanation: Ammonia is NH3, a pungent gas in which nitrogen is bonded to three hydrogen atoms.

questions.text: The chemical formula of methane is
questions.explanation: Methane, the first member of the alkane series, has one carbon bonded to four hydrogen atoms.

questions.text: Ozone is an allotrope of oxygen having the formula
questions.explanation: Ozone consists of three oxygen atoms per molecule and forms the protective layer in the stratosphere.

questions.text: Rust formed on iron is chemically
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, produced when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of moisture.

questions.text: Among metals, the best conductor of electricity is
questions.explanation: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals, though copper is used in wiring because it is cheaper.

questions.text: The most malleable and ductile metal is
questions.explanation: Gold can be beaten into extremely thin leaf and drawn into very fine wire, exceeding all other metals.

questions.text: The metal with the lowest density is
questions.explanation: Lithium has a density of about 0.53 grams per cubic centimetre, the lowest of any metal.

questions.text: The hardest naturally occurring substance is
questions.explanation: Diamond, a form of carbon with a rigid three-dimensional network of covalent bonds, tops the Mohs scale at 10.

questions.text: Sodium metal is stored under
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts violently with water and moist air, so it is kept under kerosene, with which it does not react.

questions.text: Rusting of iron takes place only in the presence of
questions.explanation: Both air and moisture are needed; iron does not rust in dry air or in air-free water.

questions.text: Galvanisation protects iron by coating it with a layer of
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron and corrodes in its place, giving sacrificial protection.

questions.text: The non-metal that conducts electricity and is used to make electrodes is
questions.explanation: In graphite each carbon uses only three of its four valence electrons for bonding, leaving delocalised electrons that carry current.

questions.text: The chief ore from which aluminium is extracted is
questions.explanation: Bauxite, a hydrated aluminium oxide, is purified to alumina and then electrolysed to obtain aluminium.

questions.text: Haematite is an important ore of
questions.explanation: Haematite is ferric oxide, Fe2O3, and is the principal ore smelted in blast furnaces to make iron.

questions.text: Cinnabar is an ore of
questions.explanation: Cinnabar is mercuric sulphide, HgS, the main natural source of mercury.

questions.text: Brass is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Brass is made mainly of copper with zinc added, which makes it harder and more workable than pure copper.

questions.text: Bronze is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Bronze is copper alloyed with tin, historically the first alloy widely used for tools and weapons.

questions.text: Steel is an alloy of iron with
questions.explanation: Ordinary steel is iron containing a small controlled percentage of carbon, which greatly increases its strength.

questions.text: The element added to steel to make it stainless is
questions.explanation: Chromium forms a thin adherent oxide film on the surface that stops further corrosion.

questions.text: Ordinary soft solder used in electrical work is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Solder is mainly tin and lead, a combination chosen for its low melting point.

questions.text: German silver is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Despite its name German silver contains no silver at all; it is copper, zinc and nickel.

questions.text: The chief constituent of the alloy duralumin is
questions.explanation: Duralumin is largely aluminium with small amounts of copper, magnesium and manganese, and is used in aircraft.

questions.text: An amalgam is an alloy in which one component is always
questions.explanation: By definition an amalgam is an alloy of mercury with another metal, as in dental fillings.

questions.text: The chief constituent of compressed natural gas is
questions.explanation: Natural gas and the CNG made from it are about 90 per cent methane.

questions.text: Liquefied petroleum gas used in domestic cylinders is mainly a mixture of
questions.explanation: LPG consists chiefly of butane and propane, which liquefy easily under moderate pressure.

questions.text: Crude petroleum is separated into petrol, kerosene and diesel by
questions.explanation: The fractions have different boiling ranges and are drawn off at different heights of a fractionating column.

questions.text: The octane number of a fuel is a measure of its
options: Ignition quality in a diesel engine
Resistance to knocking in a petrol engine
questions.explanation: A higher octane number means the petrol resists premature ignition, or knocking, in the engine cylinder.

questions.text: Water gas is a mixture of
questions.explanation: Passing steam over red-hot coke gives carbon monoxide and hydrogen, together called water gas.

questions.text: The main combustible constituent of biogas is
questions.explanation: Anaerobic digestion of organic waste yields a gas that is mostly methane, with carbon dioxide as the main diluent.

questions.text: The fuel with the highest calorific value per kilogram is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen releases roughly 150 kilojoules per gram on burning, far more than any hydrocarbon fuel.

questions.text: Incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels produces the poisonous gas
questions.explanation: With insufficient oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, which binds haemoglobin and blocks oxygen transport.

questions.text: The variety of coal with the highest carbon content is
questions.explanation: Anthracite is the most mature coal, containing over 90 per cent carbon, and burns with almost no smoke.

questions.text: The monomer from which polythene is made is
questions.explanation: Polythene is formed by addition polymerisation of ethene molecules under heat and pressure.

questions.text: The plastic abbreviated PVC is
questions.explanation: PVC stands for polyvinyl chloride, made from vinyl chloride and used for pipes, cables and sheets.

questions.text: Bakelite, used for electrical switches, is an example of a
questions.explanation: Bakelite sets permanently on moulding into a cross-linked network and cannot be softened again by heating.

questions.text: The chemical name of Teflon, used for non-stick coatings, is
questions.explanation: Teflon is polytetrafluoroethylene, whose strong carbon-fluorine bonds make it inert and slippery.

questions.text: Nylon belongs to the class of polymers called
questions.explanation: Nylon chains are joined by amide linkages, the same type of bond found in proteins.

questions.text: Vulcanisation of rubber is carried out by heating it with
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links between rubber chains, making the rubber harder, stronger and less sticky.

questions.text: The chemical formula of urea is
questions.explanation: Urea, CO(NH2)2, is made industrially from ammonia and carbon dioxide and is the world's commonest nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.text: The approximate nitrogen content of urea fertiliser is
questions.explanation: Urea contains about 46 per cent nitrogen by mass, the highest of any solid nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.text: In fertiliser grading, the letters NPK stand for
questions.explanation: N, P and K are the three major plant nutrients supplied by mixed fertilisers.

questions.text: The fertiliser DAP supplies plants with
questions.explanation: DAP is diammonium phosphate, so it provides both nitrogen and phosphorus.

questions.text: Ammonia is manufactured on an industrial scale by the
questions.explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen at high pressure over an iron catalyst to give ammonia.

questions.text: The catalyst used in the Haber process is
questions.explanation: Finely divided iron, with promoters, catalyses the combination of nitrogen and hydrogen into ammonia.

questions.text: Muriate of potash used as a fertiliser is chemically
questions.explanation: Muriate of potash is potassium chloride, KCl, the cheapest and most widely used potassium fertiliser.

questions.text: Sulphuric acid is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: In the contact process sulphur dioxide is oxidised to sulphur trioxide over a catalyst and then absorbed to give sulphuric acid.

questions.text: Sodium carbonate is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: The Solvay or ammonia-soda process makes sodium carbonate from brine, limestone and ammonia.

questions.text: Nitric acid is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: The Ostwald process oxidises ammonia over a platinum catalyst to nitrogen oxides, which are absorbed in water to give nitric acid.

questions.text: Electrolysis of concentrated brine yields caustic soda, hydrogen and
questions.explanation: In the chlor-alkali process chloride ions are oxidised at the anode to chlorine gas.

questions.text: The principal raw material used in the manufacture of ordinary glass is
questions.explanation: Glass is made by fusing silica sand with soda ash and limestone, silica being the main ingredient.

questions.text: Chlorofluorocarbons released from refrigerators and aerosols are harmful because they destroy
questions.explanation: Chlorine atoms released from CFCs by ultraviolet light break ozone molecules apart in the stratosphere.

questions.text: Bleaching powder is prepared by passing chlorine over
questions.explanation: Chlorine passed over dry calcium hydroxide gives bleaching powder, used for disinfecting and bleaching.

questions.text: Hardness of water is caused mainly by the dissolved salts of
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum, which is what makes water hard.

questions.text: Temporary hardness of water is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: Dissolved calcium and magnesium bicarbonates decompose on heating, which is why this hardness is called temporary.

questions.text: Temporary hardness of water can be removed simply by
questions.explanation: Boiling decomposes the bicarbonates into insoluble carbonates that settle out as scale.

questions.text: Municipal drinking water is commonly disinfected by adding
questions.explanation: Chlorine kills bacteria and leaves a residual that protects the water in the distribution network.

questions.text: Water has its maximum density at
questions.explanation: Water is densest at 4 degrees Celsius, which is why ice floats and ponds freeze from the top down.

questions.text: Heavy water, used as a moderator in nuclear reactors, is
questions.explanation: Heavy water is D2O, in which ordinary hydrogen is replaced by its heavier isotope deuterium.

questions.text: Electrolysis of acidified water gives hydrogen and oxygen in a volume ratio of
questions.explanation: Since water is H2O, twice as much hydrogen as oxygen is liberated by volume.

questions.text: Hard water is unsuitable for washing because it
options: Does not readily form lather with soap
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions precipitate soap as an insoluble scum instead of producing lather.

questions.text: A controlled amount of fluoride is added to drinking water or toothpaste to prevent
questions.explanation: Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel against acid attack and so reduces tooth decay.
